short_answer: Bryan Leonard is a real, long running handicapper. His WagerTalk bio says he has been a professional since 1984, moved from Cleveland to Las Vegas in 1997, and once published basketball and football newsletters. Daily Racing Form reports from 2001, 2003 and 2005 confirm that he competed in Las Vegas handicapping contests, won the regular season of the Sunset Station invitational in 2000, and finished level with the winner of a Leroy's head to head contest in 2005 before a playoff. He sells every package through WagerTalk, a large Las Vegas pick store that publishes its terms and a seller address. In that narrow sense the service is legitimate.

Whether his picks make money over time is a separate question. WagerTalk shows streaks such as "104-66 CFB Run" and "46-30 NHL Run", a list of his last 20 picks and Who's Hot boards. On 20 Nov 2026 his last 20 picks went 9 and 11. A banner says he is up 55.9 units on football this season. We found no full, time stamped log of every pick that we could check.

Independent buyer comment about him by name is almost absent. Forum members mostly pass his plays around without results, TheRX now bans posting his plays, and the complaints we found are about WagerTalk as a whole, not about him. Treat him as an experienced seller with a real contest past and marketing numbers, not a proven winner.

guarantee: On WagerTalk the guarantee is an extra cost option on daily picks. The store says "The WagerTalk pick guarantee option backs your purchase with 100% in credits." If the daily package "does not result in an overall profit across all included plays," the paid cash value is "credited back to your account to be used on a future purchase." The credit can be used on a daily package, a daily guaranteed package or any multiple day package. That is store credit, not cash.

The WagerTalk refund policy says purchases are made from Wager Talk Media, LP, that "All Sales are Final and products are sold 'as is'", and that "Once a product or service has been purchased, delivered, and/ or viewed, no refunds will be issued." It also lists cases with no refund, such as plays you cannot legally bet in your state and undelivered email or text alerts.
Nothing covers losses on the bets themselves, and those are usually far larger than the price of a pick.

claims_note: How we checked the streaks. On 17 Nov 2026 the Hot Streaks box showed 44 and 26 in the NHL, 58 and 36 in college basketball and 18 and 13 in the NBA. On 20 Nov it showed 46 and 30, 60 and 39, and 18 and 14. His last 20 list shows NHL plays from 17 to 19 Nov going 2 and 4, college basketball 2 and 3 and NBA 0 and 1, which is exactly the change. So the boxes do keep adding losses once a run is running; what they do not show is when each run started. As of 20 Nov the runs are 60.5% (NHL), 61.2% (CFB), 60.6% (CBB), 57.8% (NFL) and 56.3% (NBA).
The football banner's units add up: 35.66 in college football plus 20.24 in the NFL is 55.90. The page gives win rates but not win and loss counts, so we could not check the 62.8%.

The bio stresses low volume, but the last 20 list covers only 15 to 19 Nov 2026, including six plays on 18 Nov alone, across four sports. That is a busy schedule for a seller who calls himself selective.

The contest claims are older but have outside support. Daily Racing Form reported on 26 Dec 2001 that he had been the regular season winner of the Sunset Station invitational the year before and was 5 and 0 in the 2001 playoffs, reaching the final. On 17 Dec 2003 it reported he lost a Stardust Invitational match on a tiebreaker and was then running footballwinners.com. On 21 Dec 2005 it reported he went 4 and 3 in the final of the Leroy's Money Talks Invitational, tied with the winner, which forced a playoff. These are contest results over a few weeks, not a long term record.

An older BetFirm profile, now marked "Capper not found," described him as running Bryan Leonard Sports for 31 years and gave a 32 and 17 NFL run since late 2014 (65.3%). It is another seller page, not an audit, and it is old.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: his contest appearances in the 2000s, through Daily Racing Form reports. For his paid picks we found no full, time stamped log of every play with the line, the odds and the release time, and no court or regulator record about him.

What the seller publishes: WagerTalk lists his last 20 graded picks with odds and a result. On 20 Nov 2026 those 20 picks, from 15 to 19 Nov, went 9 wins and 11 losses: 3 and 5 in the NHL, 5 and 4 in college basketball, 1 and 1 in the NBA and 0 and 1 in the NFL. Three days earlier the same list read 11 and 9. The Who's Hot board showed him at 11 and 8 over the last 7 days and 22 and 14 over the last 30 days in college basketball. These are graded by the store that sells the picks, so they are marketing, not an audit.
His plays are copied by users into forum threads, but nobody we found keeps a long running independent tally.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Bryan Leonard pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Bryan Leonard performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the streaks on his WagerTalk profile run from about 56% to 61% winners, and his last 20 picks on 20 Nov 2026 were 45%. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Bryan Leonard is very thin. We found forum posts that copy his plays, contest coverage from the 2000s, and reviews that criticize the WagerTalk store in general. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found no buyer review, complaint or results thread about Bryan Leonard by name, positive or negative. On the Bookmakers Review forum in 2024 and on TheRX in 2026, members simply posted his plays next to other services, without saying whether they won money, and TheRX now lists him and all WagerTalk handicappers among services members must not post. The only third party praise we found is an affiliate page covered in offshore sportsbook codes. Reviews of WagerTalk itself on CapperTek, 14 of them from Mar 2021 to Jul 2026, are negative or blank, saying the store's experts lose and show only good stats, but none names him. Our saved copy of Reddit betting posts and a BBB search found nothing about him or WagerTalk. The pattern is silence rather than complaints: no billing problems and no buyer success stories.

On the Bookmakers Review forum, a member posted his Friday college football best bet, a 4% play on UNLV, with a note that his 2024 college football record was 10 and 11 at that point. No one discussed the result.

In a TheRX service play thread, a member posted two of his plays, an NHL team total and a Dodgers run line. Nobody commented. The thread header lists "All Wagertalk Cappers" and Bryan Leonard among services members are told not to post, a rule the forum first set out in Mar 2023.

CapperTek shows 14 reviews of WagerTalk. Thirteen are negative and one is blank. They say its handicappers lose overall, that advertised win rates did not match what buyers got, that support did not answer, and in one 2022 case that the buyer filed a chargeback. A Jul 2026 review said store rewards could not be redeemed. One reviewer in Jan 2026 listed WagerTalk handicappers he followed and said all lost. None of these reviews names Bryan Leonard, so they describe the store, not him.

A CappersPicks page titled "Bryan Leonard Sports Picks" says you "can't do much better" than him and his "award winning" picks, but shows no record and a "Capper not found" notice. It is surrounded by bonus codes for MyBookie, BetOnline, Bovada, XBet and SportsBetting, offshore sportsbooks, so we do not count it as a buyer view.

Our saved copy of about 820 posts from r/sportsbetting, r/sportsbook and r/SportsBettingPicks held no mention of him, and earlier archive searches on 17 Nov 2026 found nothing; a fresh archive full text search on 20 Nov timed out. A BBB search for WagerTalk returned no business profile. Web searches found no Sportsbook Review or Covers thread about his service.

conflicts: WagerTalk sells his picks and keeps the record, the Hot Streaks and the Who's Hot board that promote them. The store has a direct interest in how he looks.
The guarantee is sold by the same store and pays in store credit, which keeps a losing buyer spending there.

WagerTalk's footer says its outbound sportsbook links go only to licensed operators, but third party pages that praise him, such as CappersPicks, carry offshore sportsbook bonus codes. Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed by U.S. state regulators.
strengths: A named handicapper with a long career, and part of it, his Las Vegas contest record in the 2000s, is backed by outside news reports.
Sold by a store with written terms, a refund policy and a Las Vegas seller address.
Every package has a published price, and WagerTalk shows his last 20 graded picks with odds, losses included.
The streak boxes keep adding losses as they happen, which we confirmed against his last 20 list.
Short options such as a $39 day pass let you sample him before a long commitment.
concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw is a streak, a short board or a total chosen by the seller.
The guarantee costs extra and pays store credit, never cash, and all sales are final.
The bio says he releases only games he bets himself and favors quality over quantity, yet the profile lists 20 plays in five days.
Most contest wins and top finishes are claimed without names or years; the ones we could check are 20 or more years old.
The same football package shows two prices on one page ($449 special and $529 in the passes table).
No buyer, positive or negative, has posted a results based view of him that we could find.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Ask when each Hot Streak started. A run without a start date tells you little.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. WagerTalk's guarantee is store credit.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real handicapper with a long career, sold through WagerTalk, which publishes terms and a Las Vegas address, and news reports confirm his contest play in Las Vegas in the 2000s. We could not verify that his paid picks win over time, because no full record of every pick is public, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
How much does Bryan Leonard cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 WagerTalk sold day passes from $39, 7 days for $99, 30 days for $299 and one year for $1,999, with a one year special at $1,188. Season passes ran from $259 to $719, and a football special was $449.
Does Bryan Leonard have a verified record?

No. WagerTalk shows streaks, his last 20 picks and short leaderboards, all graded by the store that sells him. On 20 Nov 2026 his last 20 picks went 9 and 11. We found no independent, time stamped log of every pick.
Did Bryan Leonard really win handicapping contests?

Partly confirmed. Daily Racing Form reported in 2001 that he had won the regular season of the Sunset Station invitational the year before and reached the 2001 final, in 2003 that he played in the Stardust Invitational, and in 2005 that he tied for first in the Leroy's Money Talks Invitational before a playoff. We could not check his other claimed finishes.
No. WagerTalk says all sales are final. The optional guarantee, which costs extra, returns the price as store credit if a daily package does not profit.

You get every play he releases in the window you buy, from a seller with decades in the business. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays. The optional guarantee pays only store credit, and nothing covers your betting losses.
